info.name: Activityual API
info.description:
Full Activityual gateway API.

Every folder corresponds to one backend microservice. Every request includes a **human-readable description** of what it does, the **service that handles it**, and what to expect back.

**How to use:**
1. Set the `base` variable (default `http://localhost:8080`).
2. Run *Auth → Register* (only first time), then *Auth → Login* — the test script auto-fills `accessToken` and `userId` for every later request.
3. Run *Activities → Create*, copy the returned `id` into the `activityId` collection variable (auto-saved by the test script).
4. Run *Tracking → Log status* a few times, then explore Analytics / Coach / Recommendations / Notifications.

variable.description: API gateway base URL. Local: http://localhost:8080. Cloud: https://api.activityual.example.com
JWT access token. Auto-populated by the Login request.
JWT refresh token. Auto-populated by the Login request.
Logged-in user UUID. Auto-populated by the Login request.
Set automatically by Activities → Create, or fill in manually.
Set manually after listing recommendations to test the Accept endpoint.
Set manually after listing notifications to mark one as read.

item.name: Auth (auth-service · port 8081)
item.description: User registration, login, token refresh, and the current-user lookup. The only service that talks to `authdb`. Passwords are bcrypt-hashed before insert; logins return an access token (30 min) and a refresh token (7 days).

request.description:
Creates a new user. **Plain-English:** sign up with email + password and a display name. The service bcrypt-hashes the password, inserts a row in `authdb.users`, and returns the same payload as Login so the frontend can land you straight on the dashboard.

**Returns:** `{ userId, accessToken, refreshToken, displayName }`.
**Errors:** `409` if email already taken, `400` on validation failure.

exec: console.log('Saved accessToken & userId to collection vars');

request.description:
Authenticate and receive JWTs. **Plain-English:** prove who you are; in return you get a short-lived `accessToken` you put on every other request, and a longer-lived `refreshToken` you trade in when the access token expires.

**Test script** auto-fills `accessToken`, `refreshToken`, and `userId` collection variables — every later request just works.
Trade a valid refresh token for a fresh access + refresh pair. **Plain-English:** keep me logged in without asking for password again. Returns 401 if the refresh token is expired/revoked.
Returns the profile of the currently-authenticated user. **Plain-English:** ‘who am I?’ — used by the frontend to render the avatar + name in the navbar.

item.name: Activities (activity-service · port 8082)
item.description: CRUD on the user’s activity catalogue (the *what I want to track* list). Stores rows in `activitydb.activities` scoped to the JWT user. Frequency values: `DAILY`, `WEEKLY_3`, `WEEKLY_5`, `WEEKLY_7`, `CUSTOM`.

request.description: Add a new activity to track. **Plain-English:** ‘I want to do X, this often.’ Returns the persisted activity including the generated `id` — the test script saves it to `{{activityId}}` for use in later requests.
List every activity belonging to the current user. **Plain-English:** show me my catalogue. The frontend uses this on `/activities` and to populate dropdowns.
Fetch one activity. **Plain-English:** give me the details of this one habit. 404 if it doesn’t exist or belongs to someone else.
Edit an existing activity. **Plain-English:** change the title, category, frequency, or notes.
Remove an activity. **Plain-English:** I’m not doing this habit anymore. Soft-delete in the DB; the analytics service keeps history.

item.name: Tracking (tracking-service · port 8083)
item.description: Record progress and read what’s due. **This is the only service that publishes the `activity.logged` event** to RabbitMQ via the transactional outbox.

request.description:
Mark today’s entry as `done`, `missed`, or `completed`. **Plain-English:** ‘I did it’ / ‘I skipped it’ / ‘I finished the goal’.

**Internally:** inserts a row in `trackingdb.activity_logs` AND a row in `trackingdb.outbox_events` in one DB transaction. A scheduled relay then publishes the event to the RabbitMQ topic exchange `activity.events` within ~2 seconds. Four consumers react: analytics (streaks), coach (embedding into Chroma), recommendation (recompute), notification (in-app alert).
Returns the list of activities that are due today and haven’t been marked yet. **Plain-English:** ‘what do I owe myself today?’ Used by the dashboard widget.
Same as Due-today but for the rolling 7-day window. **Plain-English:** ‘what’s on my plate this week?’
Most recent log entries for the current user, newest first. **Plain-English:** ‘show me my activity history’. Powers the timeline strip on the dashboard.

item.name: Analytics (analytics-service · port 8084)
item.description: Read-only aggregates built from `activity.logged` events. Lives in `analyticsdb` as denormalised fact tables for fast reads.

request.description: Top-level dashboard numbers: total logs, done count, missed count, consistency percentage, most-consistent activity, least-consistent activity. **Plain-English:** ‘give me everything the dashboard needs in one call’.
Per-activity current and longest streak counts. **Plain-English:** ‘how many days in a row have I been doing each habit?’

item.name: Coach (coach-service · port 8085)
item.description: The AI Activity Coach — Retrieval Augmented Generation. Embeds every log into Chroma; on each question, retrieves the user’s most relevant log chunks, builds a grounded prompt, and calls Ollama (`llama3.2:3b`).

request.description:
Ask the AI Coach a free-form question. **Plain-English:** chat with a coach that has actually read your logs.

**Returns:** `{ answer: string, chunks: [{ text, timestamp, score }] }`. The frontend shows `chunks` next to the answer to prove the response is grounded in real data (no hallucination).

**Try these:**
- *Why do I keep missing my workout?*
- *What's my most consistent habit this month?*
- *Give me a plan to improve my reading streak.*

item.name: Recommendations (recommendation-service · port 8086)
item.description: Personalised timing / day-of-week / frequency suggestions. Computed by deterministic SQL heuristics over each user’s log history, recomputed on every `activity.logged` event.

request.description: Return all current recommendations for the user. **Plain-English:** ‘what should I change about my routine?’ Each item carries a `confidence` score; UI hides anything below 0.6.
Force a recompute for one activity, bypassing the event-driven path. **Plain-English:** ‘re-run the analysis right now’. Useful for testing and demos.
Mark a recommendation as accepted (or rejected). **Plain-English:** ‘yes, I’ll try that’. Stored so we can later measure whether accepted nudges actually improve completion.
Per-activity completion heatmap: matrix of day-of-week × time-of-day with completion rate per cell. **Plain-English:** ‘when am I best at this habit?’ Powers the heatmap chart on `/recommendations`.

item.name: Notifications (notification-service · port 8087)
item.description: In-app inbox. Pure event consumer — every `activity.logged` event produces a notification row in `notifdb.notifications`.

request.description: Return notifications for the user, newest first, with an unread badge count. **Plain-English:** ‘show me my inbox’.
Mark a single notification as read. **Plain-English:** ‘I’ve seen this one’.
